title: 实验 5-9 · 继电器 + 续流二极管：把线圈断电时的高压钳住
summary: GPIO → 1 kΩ → NPN 驱动 5 V 继电器线圈，线圈两端反并一个二极管；继电器触点再去开关一个 9 V 电池供电的 LED。起始电路少了二极管：每次断电，集电极被线圈冲到约 29 V。
concepts: 电感反电动势 inductive kick v = L·di/dt
NPN 驱动线圈 transistor coil driver
description: **要搭的电路**（ESP32 插在 USB 上）：
- **控制侧**：任意输出 GPIO（参考答案 GPIO4）→ R1（1 kΩ）→ Q1（2N2222）基极；E 接 GND。
- 继电器 K1 的线圈：一端接开发板 **5V** 脚，另一端接 Q1 的集电极 C。
- 续流二极管 D1 并在线圈两端：**负极（有环）接 +5 V 那一端**，正极接集电极。
- **负载侧**：9 V 电池 + → 继电器 COM；NO（常开）→ R2（1 kΩ）→ LED1 → 电池 −。电池 − 和开发板 GND 连在一起。
**起始电路**：除了 D1 都搭好了，引脚设成 10 Hz 的 PWM（继电器每秒开关 10 次，故意放大问题）。诊断会提示“K1 的线圈没有续流二极管”，时域仿真还会报告“K1 关断时产生了约 24 V 的反向电压”——集电极峰值约 **29 V**。把 D1 加上。
**引脚设置**：不用设，测试依次用输出高、输出低、PWM 10 Hz。
- 线圈 70 Ω：Ic = (4.65 − 0.21) / 70 ≈ **63 mA**（5V 脚经 USB 二极管约 4.65 V），大于 53 mA 的吸合电流，继电器吸合，COM–NO 接通。
- Ib = **2.53 mA**，强制 β = 63/2.53 ≈ 25，仍然远小于 150，Q1 饱和，Vce = **0.21 V**。（GPIO 直接驱动不了：3.3 V 只能给线圈 47 mA，还远超引脚 20 mA 的建议值。）
- 输出低：Q1 截止，线圈没电，继电器释放，LED 灭。
- PWM 10 Hz、**有 D1**：集电极最高只到 **5.37 V**（5V 脚电压 + 二极管压降）。没有 D1：断电瞬间线圈电流 63 mA 无处可去，v = L·di/dt 把集电极推到约 **29 V**。
**续流二极管怎么工作**：通电时 D1 反偏，不起作用。断电时线圈“想”维持原来的电流方向，于是它下端（集电极）电压升高；一旦比 +5 V 高 0.7 V，D1 导通，电流沿“线圈 → D1 → 线圈”的小回路慢慢衰减（时间常数 L/R = 150 mH / 70 Ω ≈ 2 ms），能量变成热量消耗在线圈电阻和二极管上。
**要测什么、为什么**：继电器吸合 / 释放和 LED；Q1 饱和；线圈电流 ≈ 63 mA；PWM 时用示波器看集电极 Vmax ≈ 5.4 V，证明高压被钳住了。
**实际项目经验**：
- 买到的“5 V 继电器模块”板上已经有三极管、续流二极管和指示灯（有的还有光耦）；裸继电器才要自己搭。很多模块是**低电平触发**（IN 接 GND 时吸合）。
- 5 V 继电器线圈从 5V / VIN 取电，不要从 3V3 取；3.3 V 的模块要买“3 V 线圈”的版本。
- 二极管用 1N4007 / 1N4148 就够了。它让继电器释放慢一点（几毫秒）；对释放速度有要求时，串一个齐纳二极管加快能量消耗。
- 触点能切交流 250 V / 10 A 也不代表面包板可以——接市电要用带外壳的模块、保持安全间距，初学者不要碰 220 V。
- 这里电池 − 和 GND 连在一起；继电器真正的优点是触点和线圈**电气隔离**，负载侧可以完全不共地。
- ESP32 别用 GPIO0/2/5/12/15 驱动继电器，开机时会“咔哒”一下。
**模型说明**：线圈是 70 Ω + 150 mH，电流 ≥ 53 mA 吸合、< 7 mA 释放，没有机械动作时间。没有二极管时仿真的尖峰约 29 V（受仿真步长和三极管关断过程限制），真实电路里还可能更高，直到三极管 C–E 击穿（约 40 V）。仿真目前要求负载电池的 − 和开发板 GND 相连（两个独立的“地”会被合并，见报告）。

en.title: Experiment 5-9 · Relay + flyback diode: clamp the coil's turn-off spike
en.summary: GPIO → 1 kΩ → NPN drives a 5 V relay coil with a diode reversed across it; the relay contact switches an LED powered by a 9 V battery. The starting board lacks the diode: every turn-off kicks the collector to about 29 V.
description: **What you build** (ESP32 on USB):
- **Control side**: any output GPIO (the reference uses GPIO4) → R1 (1 kΩ) → base of Q1 (2N2222); E to GND.
- Relay K1's coil: one end to the board's **5V** pin, the other to Q1's collector C.
- Flyback diode D1 across the coil: **cathode (band) to the +5 V end**, anode to the collector.
- **Load side**: 9 V battery + → relay COM; NO (normally open) → R2 (1 kΩ) → LED1 → battery −. The battery − is joined to the board's GND.

**Starting board**: everything except D1 is built, and the pin is set to 10 Hz PWM (the relay clicks 10 times a second, to exaggerate the problem). The diagnostics say "K1's coil has no flyback diode", and the time-domain simulation reports "K1 kicks back about 24 V when it switches off" — the collector peaks at about **29 V**. Add D1.
**Pin table settings**: nothing to set; the tests use output HIGH, output LOW and 10 Hz PWM.
**Numbers (simulated)**:
- Coil 70 Ω: Ic = (4.65 − 0.21) / 70 ≈ **63 mA** (the 5V pin is about 4.65 V after the USB diode), above the 53 mA pull-in current: the relay pulls in and COM–NO closes.

- Ib = **2.53 mA**, forced β = 63/2.53 ≈ 25, still far below 150, so Q1 saturates with Vce = **0.21 V**. (A GPIO can't drive the coil directly: 3.3 V gives only 47 mA, and that is way above the pin's 20 mA recommendation anyway.)
- Load side: (9 − 2.1) / 1 kΩ ≈ **6.8 mA**, the green LED is on.
- Output LOW: Q1 is cut off, the coil is unpowered, the relay drops out and the LED goes off.

- PWM 10 Hz **with D1**: the collector peaks at only **5.37 V** (the 5V pin plus one diode drop). Without D1 the 63 mA coil current has nowhere to go at turn-off and v = L·di/dt drives the collector to about **29 V**.

**How the flyback diode works**: while the coil is on, D1 is reverse-biased and does nothing. At turn-off the coil "wants" to keep its current flowing the same way, so its lower end (the collector) rises; as soon as it is 0.7 V above +5 V, D1 conducts and the current decays around the small loop coil → D1 → coil (time constant L/R = 150 mH / 70 Ω ≈ 2 ms), its energy turning into heat in the coil resistance and the diode.
**What you measure and why**: relay on/off and the LED; Q1 saturated; coil current ≈ 63 mA; with PWM the scope's Vmax on the collector ≈ 5.4 V, proof that the spike is clamped.
**Rule of thumb for real projects**:

- A ready-made "5 V relay module" already carries the transistor, flyback diode and an indicator LED (some add an opto-coupler); only a bare relay needs you to build this. Many modules are **active-low** (they pull in when IN is tied to GND).
- Power a 5 V relay coil from 5V / VIN, never from 3V3; for a 3.3 V system buy the "3 V coil" version.
- A 1N4007 / 1N4148 is plenty. It makes the relay release a little slower (a few ms); where release speed matters, add a Zener in series to dump the energy faster.
- Contacts rated 250 V AC / 10 A do not make a breadboard mains-safe — mains needs an enclosed module and proper clearances; beginners shouldn't touch 230 V.
- Here the battery − shares GND; the real strength of a relay is that the contacts are **galvanically isolated** from the coil, so the load side needs no common ground at all.
- Don't drive a relay from ESP32 GPIO0/2/5/12/15 — it will click during boot.

**Model note**: the coil is 70 Ω + 150 mH, pulling in at ≥ 53 mA and releasing below 7 mA, with no mechanical delay. Without the diode the simulated spike is about 29 V (limited by the time step and the transistor's turn-off); a real circuit can go higher, up to the transistor's C–E breakdown (about 40 V). The simulator currently needs the load battery's − joined to the board GND (two separate "grounds" get merged — see report).
hints: The diode goes across the coil, band (cathode) on the 5V end, plain end (anode) on the collector.
Coil between the 5V pin and C; E to GND; GPIO → 1 kΩ → B.
Load: battery + → COM, NO → 1 kΩ → LED → battery −; join battery − to the board GND.
tests: Output HIGH: relay pulls in, LED on, Q1 saturated, coil ≈ 63 mA
Output LOW: relay released, LED off, Q1 cut off
PWM 10 Hz: with D1 the collector peaks at only ≈ 5.4 V (spike clamped)

tests.name: 输出高：继电器吸合，LED 亮，Q1 饱和，线圈 ≈ 63 mA
输出低：继电器释放，LED 灭，Q1 截止
PWM 10 Hz：有 D1 时集电极最高只有 ≈ 5.4 V（尖峰被钳住）

hints: 二极管并在线圈两端：有环的一端（负极）接 5V 那头，另一端（正极）接集电极。
线圈接在 5V 脚和 C 之间；E 接 GND；GPIO → 1 kΩ → B。
负载侧：电池 + → COM，NO → 1 kΩ → LED → 电池 −；电池 − 接开发板 GND。
